question: Blood cultures are sent to the laboratory. Antibiotic treatment is started. Blood cultures confirm an infection with methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus epidermidis. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.opa: Oral penicillin V + gentamicin for 4 weeks
options.opb: Intravenous ampicillin + rifampin + ceftriaxone for 2 weeks
options.ope: Intravenous nafcillin + rifampin for 6 weeks + gentamicin for 2 weeks

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus epidermidis infection -> susceptible to beta-lactam antibiotics -> 90% CHAIN: Methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus epidermidis infection -> treat with beta-lactam antibiotics -> 85% CHAIN: Methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus epidermidis infection -> not resistant to penicillin -> treat with penicillin -> 80% CHAIN: Methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus epidermidis infection -> not resistant to penicillin -> treat with penicillin + gentamicin -> 90%
analysis: The most appropriate next step in management for an infection with methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus epidermidis would be to treat with intravenous nafcillin + rifampin for 6 weeks + gentamicin for 2 weeks. This combination provides effective coverage against Staphylococcus epidermidis.
